reviews.title: Good for the price.
reviews.comment: Basically got the best mouse on the market for 70 dollars even though it didn’t come with the 8k hz polling dongle, but I can always buy that from a third party source somewhere. The mouse feels great in the hand, feels very responsive, and there’s little to no delay. The software is easy to use and changing the dpi could be better but the fact it even has the button on it is great for functionality purposes. Nothing better for this value.
reviews.author: Dawn Campello

reviews.title: Holds a charge & lightweight
reviews.comment: My husband loves this mouse. It holds a charge well. He says it fits well in his hand & is easy to use. It is very sensitive to movements. It's super lightweight also
reviews.author: teresa

reviews.title: A perfect mouse... if not for one HUGE problem.
reviews.comment:
This mouse is amazing. Light, ergonomic, a great battery... however the scroll wheel is just completely defective.
The first renewed Deathadder v3 Pro I received had a faulty scroll wheel, so they kindly offered for me to return it and get a new one. I did so, and the scroll wheel was a little better, but now a few weeks later it is just the worst. It will not scroll, or will scroll the wrong direction more often than it will do what you want it to do. Upon further research it seems this is a common problem with this mouse. Tech savvy folks can buy a new encoder for the scroll wheel, take it apart, replace and sodder in the new encoder which seems to work well but that's a little out of my depth.
I wonder if a brand new one would work well at first and then degrade into what my used one is now. Hopefully this is fixed at some point because it's so disappointing to have such a glaring issue on the otherwise best mouse I have ever owned.
reviews.author: Xander

reviews.title: A great deal with a couple of downsides.
reviews.comment: getting this mouse nearly 50% off was an excellent deal - But this was not "refurbished" from the seller I got it from. It was definitely an open box return that was used. there was a lot of *grime* in the crevices that was easily cleaned with rubbing alcohol and a cleaning brush. The Scroll wheel is a bit glitchy and skips at slower speeds. I'll probably have to pull the mouse apart to clean the encoder properly. The skates on my unit were still in great shape and I don't see a need to replace them with dots any time soon. The grip on this shape is excellent if you like ergo shapes. The only thing missing in the box for me was the grips, but who cares, those can be had for a dime a dozen these days if you like them. I don't care about grips, so it's no issue for me. I took one star off because of how filthy the mouse was, and I took another star off because of the dirty encoder that I'll have to clean out. But, overall, I'm still happier buying this for $70 than spending $150 on a new one. Just be prepared to clean up a bunch of gross dead skin that's built up in the crevices - and I hope you don't get one with a dirty encoder on the scroll wheel because pulling this apart just to clean it is going to be less than fun.
reviews.author: cathy koltun

reviews.title: Great mouse, terrible mouse wheel encoder
reviews.comment: Mouse is great except for the known scroll wheel failure issue. They use a Kailh encoder for the mouse wheel that fails pretty quickly. I got a warranty replacement from Razer that also failed, so I replaced the encoder myself with a TTC Gold 15mm encoder, threw some glass skates on it, and it's now the best gaming mouse I've ever owned.
reviews.author: Marco C
